When I look at a bubble closely, I see swirling iridescence. Why/how does this happen?

The soap from a bubble acts as a prism for the sunlight, causing the different colors' wavelengths to separate. As gravity pulls on the bubble, more of the soap falls down the sides of the bubble, causing the thickness of the bubble, and therefore the prism, to change, resulting in swirling.

Thin film interference.

Thin "films" of material refract different wavelengths (colours) of light differently. The surface of a bubble changes as the soap naturally moves towards the bottom (gravity). If it happens evenly, you see a smooth rainbow of colours. If it happens unevenly, you get swirls of colour.

Jules Bianchi succumbs to his injuries.
The first accidental death in Formula 1 since Imola, 1994, when we lost Roland Ratzenberger and Ayrton Senna on the same weekend.

Horrible that it happened but I'm glad that we are improving safety with the virtual safety car. It means that his death wasn't fully in vain. The FIA waited for FAR more deaths over the years before changing things significantly.

This is rough, I wasn't alive for the Senna days, and to be honest through my life I had subconsiouly accepted the idea that F1 drivers were pretty much invincible when they were in their cars at a Grand Prix thanks to the survival cells, and the advances in modern medicine. This whole time I was thinking "it's terrible he's had a crash and he probably won't drive again, but at least he'll wake up". It instills a renewed fear for the life of Michael Schumacher.

I think it shows that we can't get too complacent, ever. Even if we have Robert Kubica and others walking away from some of the most violent crashes seen in the sport, there will always be something we can do to reduce absurd risks while maintaining the essence of the Formula. The worst part is that this crash was caused by a danger that has been pointed out multiple times by members of our community such as Martin Brundle. We need to do more to be proactive rather than reactive. I know many people say this post-disastrous event, but I remembered specifically reading news about the storm passing through and the race maintaining it's time on the Friday, and having an "off" feeling about the whole weekend.

I know many probably don't care about my opinion on the topic, but I felt I needed to write something about it. It's tragic that we lost not just a driver, but such an extraordinary young man with the brightest of futures ahead of him.

Forza Jules.
